Will —

Thanks — attaching a MAP and a token-econ workbook to populate. High level notes up front so you can run scenarios quickly: 

- Baseline model: 1.2M requests / month, average 20 tokens generated per request (short chat), average 15 tokens in prompt. Model used: rwd-4.1-large quantized; baseline price = $0.0008 per output-token (hosted), input tokens priced at 50% of output.
- Caching assumptions: prefix caching for repeated prompts (expected cache hit 7% for scripted workflows).
- Batching: we assume dynamic batching with a 25ms coalescing window for the Hosted tier; effective throughput improves token cost by ~8% at 95th p99 latency SLO. For Dedicated, batching gains vary with pool size — see workbook tab 'batching-sensitivity'.
- KV cache: for chat flows we assume per-conversation KV reuse. If you plan to truncate history aggressively, token usage drops ~12% in our sims.
- Eval plan: we recommend a 2-week eval against 3 prompt families (triage, summarization, followup) with automated quality checks (ROUGE/semantic sim) and a token-cost reconciliation run at 1 week.

I included a short MAP plan with milestones to get to PO and pilot kickoff, plus the workbook (crestline_token_model.xlsx) with scenario tabs: 'monthly-baseline', 'burst-sensitivity', 'quantization-impact', 'batching-cache'. Fill in the left column with your expected session length distribution and burst profile.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You populate session-length buckets in the workbook and share it back by Wed EOD.
2) We run a joint token-cost simulation and share a verified per-token / per-eval summary.
3) Sign MAP and DocuSign PO; pilot kickoff within 2 weeks of signature.

Marcus / team —

Quick ops notes to put in the MAP appendix (technical assumptions):

- Batching: our internal tests use dynamic batching with adaptive windowing. For a 250-GPU Dedicated pool we see ~10-12% token-cost improvement on average; on Hosted the improvement is 6-9% depending on QPS shape. Workbook includes conservative (6%) and optimistic (12%) columns.
- Prefix/KV caching: we recommend enabling prefix cache with a 10k-entry LRU and a 24-hour TTL for your pilot. Cache hit % is highly sensitive to prompt variety — I added a 'cache-sensitivity' slider in the workbook.
- Quantization: rwd-4.1-large (8-bit) gives ~1.6x throughput improvement vs fp16 in our workload and minimal quality delta for short chat bursts; included a 'quantized' price multiplier in the workbook (0.65x cost).
- Tail latencies: if your p95 SLA is under 200ms, we should disable aggressive batching; workbook has a column for latency-constrained cost.

I'll run a dry run of the 1.2M monthly baseline tonight and post numbers tomorrow morning.
